workflow_sequence.description: Workflow receives an EDD preflight request carrying a repository anchor, optional explicit target root, scoped paths, target skill, required test cases, deterministic evaluation command, execution provider, and iteration/token limits.

handshake_points.data_shape: object with anchor_path, explicit_root, scoped_paths, skill_name, evaluation_config, provider, limits, lease_policy

workflow_sequence.description: Resolve one canonical Git worktree from the anchor and any explicit root, rejecting missing anchors or conflicting roots before any further validation.

handshake_points.data_shape: realpath absolute worktree root, branch or detached state, and starting commit SHA

workflow_sequence.description: Canonicalize every scoped input, skill, evaluation, and authorized-scope path and verify it is contained by the resolved worktree, rejecting parent-directory or symlink traversal that escapes it.

handshake_points.data_shape: list of normalized absolute paths and a containment result

workflow_sequence.description: Inspect Git status and reject the request if staged, unstaged, or untracked changes exist outside configured scratch directories.

handshake_points.data_shape: status summary including modified, staged, untracked, and scratch-ignored flags

workflow_sequence.description: Confirm the target skill and its evaluation suite exist in the target repository.

handshake_points.data_shape: boolean existence and filesystem location of the skill and its evaluation suite

workflow_sequence.description: Acquire a repository-scoped mutation lease for the resolved worktree under the configured concurrency policy.

handshake_points.data_shape: lease token with repo key, run id, acquired_at, and TTL

workflow_sequence.description: Record the validated target repository context and starting revision, then return it to the workflow for use by all downstream activities.
On any validation or lease failure, report every failed condition and release any acquired lease without starting refinement.

handshake_points.data_shape: PreflightFailureReport with failed_conditions and released_lease flag

instrumentation_events.description: Emitted when a target worktree is discovered from an anchor or explicit root.

data_points.description: HEAD commit SHA at preflight time

instrumentation_events.description: Emitted after all scoped paths are canonicalized and checked for containment.

data_points.description: Paths that resolve outside the worktree

instrumentation_events.description: Emitted when Git status is inspected for cleanness.
Emitted when the repository-scoped mutation lease is acquired.

data_points.description: Workflow run id holding the lease

instrumentation_events.description: Emitted when a lease is released, including on failure cleanup.

data_points.description: Workflow run id that held the lease

instrumentation_events.description: Emitted at the end of preflight with the aggregate result.

new_responsibilities.intent: The requester must see a clear report of what passed and what failed.

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Adapt the request form based on the caller's role
new_responsibilities.intent: Role may determine whether explicit root or advanced limits are exposed, but not enforce them.

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Resolve the nearest Git worktree from the anchor or explicit root
new_responsibilities.intent: Git root discovery logic is in the defensible zone and must not depend on client path manipulation.

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Canonicalize and validate all repository-scoped paths
new_responsibilities.intent: Security enforcement and path traversal prevention belong in the backend.

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Inspect repository status and enforce clean-worktree policy
new_responsibilities.intent: Only the backend can safely execute git status and decide whether to mutate.

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Discover the target skill and its evaluation suite
new_responsibilities.intent: Business logic for whether a skill is present and runnable.

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Apply the repository-scoped mutation lease policy
new_responsibilities.intent: Concurrency and lease duration are business rules.

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Release any acquired lease on failure
new_responsibilities.intent: Operational safety and correctness of the lease contract.

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Persist mutation leases and enforce uniqueness by repository key
new_responsibilities.intent: The lease store is the source of truth for concurrent access.

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Store the preflight result and target repository context
new_responsibilities.intent: Provides an auditable record and a hand-off artifact for downstream activities.

architectural_decisions.decision: Resolve the nearest Git worktree using git rev-parse --show-toplevel from the anchor, and compare it with an optional explicit root after canonicalization.
architectural_decisions.justification: The nearest containing worktree is deterministic and matches ADR-018. Canonicalization before comparison catches relative, absolute, and symlinked forms that refer to the same worktree.
architectural_decisions.basis: ADR-018: Explicit Target Repository Context for Agentic Workflows
architectural_decisions.impact: New TargetWorktreeResolver in src/common; change to SkillActivityInput to accept target context.
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: What is the canonicalization policy for repository and scope paths?

architectural_decisions.decision: Canonicalize all repository-scoped paths using Path.resolve() (realpath + absolute) and verify containment with Path.relative_to against the target root.
architectural_decisions.justification: Path.resolve() removes symlinks and parent-directory traversal in one step. relative_to raises ValueError for paths outside the root, which is a simple and platform-aware containment check.
architectural_decisions.basis: ADR-018 and filesystem path normalization best practices
architectural_decisions.impact: New ScopedPathValidator in src/common; validation is performed before any skill is invoked.
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: What is the canonicalization policy for repository and scope paths?

architectural_decisions.decision: Acquire the mutation lease only after all other preconditions pass.
architectural_decisions.justification: This ordering avoids lock churn and unnecessary contention. Because the lease is the final step, there is no later validation that could require its release under normal flow.
architectural_decisions.basis: Lease acquisition best practice and the story acceptance criteria
architectural_decisions.impact: Preflight validator executes checks in a strict sequence; any failure before the lease step does not touch the lease store.
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: If preflight acquires the lease and then a later check fails, is lease release guaranteed even if the workflow process crashes?

architectural_decisions.decision: Persist mutation leases with a short TTL and release them explicitly on every terminal path, with TTL as a fail-safe.
architectural_decisions.justification: A TTL guarantees that a crashed worker cannot hold a lease indefinitely. Explicit release in a try/finally block keeps the common case fast and auditable.
architectural_decisions.basis: ADR-018 and Cadence activity retry safety patterns
architectural_decisions.impact: LeaseStore schema requires repo_key, run_id, acquired_at, and expires_at; workflow wraps the lease in a context manager.
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: How long does a repository-scoped mutation lease remain valid, and what triggers automatic release?

architectural_decisions.decision: Use an immediate-reject concurrency policy when another run holds the lease for the same repository.
architectural_decisions.justification: Immediate reject is the simplest policy to implement and reason about. Wait queues and force-after-grace can be added later without changing the lease store schema.
architectural_decisions.basis: Open concurrency question in the story analysis
architectural_decisions.impact: LeaseStore.acquire returns a conflict rather than blocking; the workflow maps this to a failed precondition.
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: What is the concurrency policy when another run holds the lease?

architectural_decisions.decision: Allow a configured scratch or process directory to be ignored in dirty-worktree checks only when all unexpected changes are confined to that directory.
architectural_decisions.justification: This lets the workflow write operational artifacts without failing its own preflight, while still detecting changes outside the controlled area.
architectural_decisions.basis: Open scratch-directory question in the story analysis
architectural_decisions.impact: RepositoryStatusInspector accepts a scratch_globs list; git status results are filtered before producing the clean/dirty verdict.
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: Which files or directories are treated as scratch or process output that may be ignored in dirty-worktree checks?

architectural_decisions.decision: Preflight validates the presence of the target skill and its evaluation suite, but not the syntactic or semantic correctness of test cases or the evaluation command.
architectural_decisions.justification: Semantic validation belongs to the refinement and execution steps. Preflight is a safety gate, not a deep parser, and should reject fast on missing prerequisites.
architectural_decisions.basis: Open validation-depth question in the story analysis and the skills-based architecture in ADR-003
architectural_decisions.impact: SkillAndEvaluationDiscovery checks for the expected skill directory and evaluation suite; detailed parsing is left to downstream activities.
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: Should preflight validate that the required test cases and evaluation command are syntactically or semantically valid, or only that they are present?

questions_addressed.question: What is the canonicalization policy for repository and scope paths?
questions_addressed.answer: Use Path.resolve() to obtain the real, absolute path, then compare using Path.relative_to. Case sensitivity follows the underlying filesystem.
questions_addressed.justification: Realpath plus absolute removes symlinks, relative components, and parent-directory traversal in one step. relative_to gives a simple containment test.

questions_addressed.question: How long does a repository-scoped mutation lease remain valid, and what triggers automatic release?
questions_addressed.answer: The lease has a configurable TTL. It is explicitly released on every terminal path, and the TTL provides an automatic expiry if the worker crashes.
questions_addressed.justification: Explicit release is fast and auditable; TTL is a fail-safe against orphaned leases.
questions_addressed.basis: Architectural decision 4 in this design document

questions_addressed.question: What is the concurrency policy when another run holds the lease?
questions_addressed.answer: Immediate reject. Queuing and force-after-grace are deferred to future work.
questions_addressed.justification: The simplest policy that satisfies the AC and can be extended later.
questions_addressed.basis: Architectural decision 5 in this design document

questions_addressed.question: If preflight acquires the lease and then a later check fails, is lease release guaranteed even if the workflow process crashes?
questions_addressed.answer: The lease is the final preflight check, so no later validation can fail after acquisition. A workflow-level try/finally releases the lease on terminal paths, and the TTL limits the impact of a crash.
questions_addressed.justification: Moving acquisition last removes the failure-after-lease scenario from the normal path; the combination of explicit release and TTL handles the exception path.
questions_addressed.basis: Architectural decision 3 in this design document

questions_addressed.question: Which files or directories are treated as scratch or process output that may be ignored in dirty-worktree checks?
questions_addressed.answer: A configurable list of scratch or process-directory globs, defaulting to the target repository's .process/ directory, may be ignored when all unexpected changes are confined to those globs.
questions_addressed.justification: Operational artifacts must not fail preflight, but changes outside the controlled area must still be rejected.
questions_addressed.basis: Architectural decision 6 in this design document

questions_addressed.question: Should preflight validate that the required test cases and evaluation command are syntactically or semantically valid, or only that they are present?
questions_addressed.answer: Preflight only checks presence, not syntactic or semantic validity.
questions_addressed.justification: Preflight is a fast safety gate. Deep validation is a refinement concern and will fail with meaningful feedback during execution.
questions_addressed.basis: Architectural decision 7 in this design document
